newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tempo of Japan recovery slow, needs vigilance - PM.
newsitem.headline: Tempo of Japan recovery slow, needs vigilance - PM.

text.p: The pace of Japan's economic recovery remains slow and it still needs careful vigilance, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday.

In a speech to a convention of securities brokerages, Hashimoto said: "Fortunately, the private sector is increasing its strength and the economy continues to recover. However, at the moment the tempo is gradual and the jobs situation is still severe despite some improvement."
He added: "It is necessary to closely watch the future direction of the economy." The speech was delivered by a senior official at the Prime Minister's Office.

An ageing society and the globalisation of economies meant Japan must change its "overall system" and press forward with structural reforms in its economy, administration and society, the prime minister said in the speech.
Hashimoto also cited the need for structural reforms in the nation's fiscal budget, which he said was in a worse condition than that of any other major industrialised nation.
Japan also needed to ensure a more transparent financial system, better use of land and further deregulation in order to rebuild a strong economy in the medium to longer term, he said.
The prime minister also called for reforms in the domestic stock market in the long term. Japan's stock market has been stagnant compared with other major markets overseas, he said.

The government would carry out wide-ranging reforms in the domestic stock market in order to improve its functions and ensure necessary funds for companies as well as to meet diversifying demand from investors, Hashimoto said.
